Northwind Bikes: Annual Report 2025
Northwind Bikes is a small bicycle company based in Leeds. It sells
city bikes and electric bikes online and through two shops. This
report covers the year from January to December 2025. It is a
practice document made for testing AI tools. All names and
numbers are made up.

 A message from the founder
This was our busiest year so far. We opened a second shop,
launched a repair subscription, and grew online sales. We also had
problems: a supplier delay in spring and higher shipping costs in
the autumn. This report explains both the good news and the
problems.

 Sales
Total revenue in 2025 was 4.2 million pounds, up from 3.5 million
pounds in 2024. That is growth of 20 percent. Online sales made
up 58 percent of revenue. The two shops made up the other 42
percent.

 Products
We sold 3,100 bikes in total. Electric bikes were 1,240 of them,
which is 40 percent of all bikes sold. The best-selling model was
the Commuter E2 electric bike, with 610 units sold.

 The new shop
Our second shop opened in York on 14 June 2025. It cost 180,000
pounds to open. By December it was making a small profit each
month. We plan to keep both shops open in 2026.

 Repair subscription
In March we launched Northwind Care, a repair subscription that
costs 9 pounds a month. By the end of the year it had 820
members. Members get two free services a year and 20 percent off
parts.

 Problems this year
In April, our main frame supplier delayed deliveries by six weeks.
About 300 orders arrived late. We gave every affected customer a
25 pound voucher. Shipping costs also rose by 12 percent in the
autumn.

 Customers
Our customer satisfaction score was 4.6 out of 5, based on 2,900
reviews. The most common complaint was delivery time. The most
common praise was for our repair team.

 Team
We ended the year with 46 staff, up from 38. Twelve of them work
in repairs. We trained six new bike mechanics through our own
training programme.

 Plans for 2026
In 2026 we plan to launch a cargo e-bike, find a second frame
supplier so one delay cannot stop us, and grow Northwind Care to
2,000 members. We do not plan to open a third shop in 2026.
